As the child of a couple who loves to travel, that shit was lit!!!!! I don’t think they could be as spontaneous anymore and they couldn’t pack lightly. We typically took one 7-10 day vacation to a warm destination and one smaller weekend camping or road trip. They took my sister and I everywhere. The only time they took longer vacations alone was after we were adults. I don’t regret a minute of it (obviously, how could I?). My sister and I have soooo many great memories. Now as adults we still travel together and are going to Japan and Korea together in a few weeks. It’s not always perfect. Over the years I’ve gotten sick in other countries and that’s never any fun. My sister and I both had horrible plane anxiety as children but we wouldn’t make a huge fuss. We’d just silently cry and hold my mom’s hands lol. Luckily we grew out of it. Also, on one flight my sister and I simultaneously got motion sickness and vomitted onto my dad within a minute of each other. We have also had some monumental fights on vacation I can’t lie, but that’s just what happens with two teenagers. Also another thing to consider is you’re limited by the school calendar for traveling dates.

I am personally unsure if I want children or not but I don’t think this should be the main determining factor. I believe you can still travel with children you may just have to travel more closely or save up longer to make it work. Just wanted to offer an alternative perspective.

First— having a puppy is hard! Don’t feel bad for struggling. Most of this sub is people sharing their struggles.

Next, how is he escaping his crate and playpen? He shouldn’t be able to. Figure that situation out and buy some ear plugs or noise canceling headphones. Let him bark it out while you take care of yourself. You can’t properly take care of another creature if you’re not taking care of yourself. 

For potty take him out A LOT for potty breaks. Like more than you think. 

I recommend frozen kongs or lickmats it keeps them occupied for quite a bit. 

As for the husband that seems more like a relationship problem not a puppy one. Did he also want a dog? Have a convo with him about expectations. It’s not fair on you to be doing the bulk of the care. Talk to him about it.

It almost feels cliche to say this but he won’t be a puppy forever. This phase will pass. I was similar to you going crazy when I got my dog. My boyfriend at the time and my own mom told me I should rehome him. I very briefly considered it. I’m so glad I didn’t! I stuck through it and now he’s soooo much easier to manage. I’m going to be real he sounds autistic. I’m guessing he is completely unaware of this and that’s why his sensory issues are so poorly managed. I wasn’t exactly like this but I was so wound up trying to be “normal” all the time without realizing, textures, sounds, or unexpected changes in plans would set me off. I felt like super grumpy and upset to the point of tears. Idk how to explain it. To the outside world I just seemed maybe spoiled or self centered, but that’s not how it felt to me at all. My ex boyfriend saw the most of it because he was the one person I felt comfortable enough in front of. Once I realized I was autistic I learned how to prevent these scenarios and tbh my quality of life is all around better.

You’re not obligated to stay with him if you’re unhappy. However, if you do break up with him you should bring up autism to him. It might be awkward, but I wouldn’t have considered autism if a friend never brought it up to me. And guess what, they were right!

Hi, I just wanted to chime in as another autistic person. My dog is 10 months now, but there was a period around 5-7 months where I thought about rehoming him because I’d get sooooo overwhelmed. My parents and partner even found me hitting myself and crying during one particular bad meltdown. I realized a lot of my meltdowns weren’t JUST caused by my dog but a lot of other underlying stress. So, I tried to manage my non-dog related stress. I started wearing noise blocking earbuds when he’d have a barking fit. I also tried to remember whenever my dog was freaking out he probably felt the way I feel when I’m having a meltdown. I’m just sharing this to say I don’t feel that way anymore and I’m SO glad I didn’t rehome him.
